extracted.intended_audience: mathematics instructors and educators (K–12 and postsecondary), especially those seeking to teach more equitably in the US context
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and evaluative criteria for designing and enacting mathematics instruction that disrupts classroom hierarchies and centers access, belonging, and equitable participation. Includes classroom structures, question-asking, assessment approaches, equity analytics (EQUIP), and professional learning strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access means that everyone can exist in a space in their full humanity and have their varied needs respected and met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring access is both a matter of accessible design (i.e., flexible practices that generally work for a lot of different people), and specific accommodations for individual needs that are not adequately addressed by your overall design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The things that an individual needs to access a space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access needs are many and can be varied, including: 1. Physical access and ergonomics; 2. Opportunities to move, stretch, and take breaks; 3. Food, drinks, appropriate bathrooms; 4. Language/communication that is understandable; 5. Safety, trust, and nonjudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible syllabus and design
rubrics_metrics.description: Syllabus and course design should be intentionally created to maximize access and consider movement/physical access, accommodations, and flexible assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accessible design language, explicit accommodations processes, normalize access talk, design flexible assessments and movement-friendly classrooms, and ensure syllabus communicates community norms and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Classrooms in which students engage in a variety of activities (as compared to pure lecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active-learning strategies while attending to equity: active learning can increase engagement but may also be inequitable if structures do not distribute participation and status fairly. Make active learning more equitable by structuring tasks, roles, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-worthy tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks used to engage students in deep learning with problems that require multiple minds to meaningfully engage with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks that require collaboration, multiple perspectives, and cannot be trivially completed by an individual, so groups have genuine opportunities to contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice and design of mathematical tasks used in class to elicit student thinking and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize tasks that are meaningful, promote productive struggle, elicit mathematical practices, are accessible (language/design), and support group-worthy collaborative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities and behaviors that reflect authentic mathematical work (e.g., reasoning, conjecturing, explaining, justifying).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks and classroom interactions to foreground mathematical practices rather than rote procedures, and support students in engaging with those practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalizing failure and productive struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Classroom cultures and practices that treat failure and struggle as normal and productive parts of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly normalize struggle, scaffold tasks to make productive struggle possible, model how to persist, and avoid signaling that immediate correctness is the only valued outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistemologies of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The classroom framing of what mathematics is, who does mathematics, and how mathematical knowledge is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt epistemologies that humanize mathematics (e.g., multiple ways of knowing, culturally relevant examples) rather than portraying mathematics as fixed, neutral, or only accessible to a narrow group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanizing through role models
rubrics_metrics.description: Using diverse role models and narratives to make mathematics feel more human and accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include role models that reflect students' identities, histories, and cultures to counteract stereotypes about who can be a mathematician.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deconstructing stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit instructional work to reveal and challenge harmful stereotypes about mathematics and learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discourse, examples, and data to confront stereotypes, and create space for students to question and reinterpret common cultural narratives about ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships: Authenticity and knowing your students
rubrics_metrics.description: Build authentic relationships by knowing students as people and as mathematicians and by regularly checking in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly collect information about students' lives, identities, and mathematical backgrounds; use that knowledge to inform instruction, show care, and tailor supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community agreements and revisiting agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish explicit community agreements that govern classroom interactions and revisit them regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-create agreements with students, make them visible, and revisit to ensure they remain relevant; include community-building activities and fun to sustain engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group composition and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing groups with attention to composition (who is grouped with whom) and explicit roles to distribute status and work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to social markers and skills when composing groups, rotate roles, and assign roles that create participation opportunities for lower-status students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structures for participation (individual/partners/groups/whole-class)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of participation structures (individual work, partners, groups, whole-class) to engage students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose structures intentionally based on goals, use pre-briefs and debriefs, scaffold group work, and ensure accountability so contributions are distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional participation structures (gallery walk, paper toss, whiteboards, virtual structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific active-learning structures used to surface student thinking and distribute participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gallery walks to share work publicly, paper toss for rapid sampling, whiteboards for visible work, and adapt structures for virtual environments to maintain equitable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning strategies (inviting and deepening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask a variety of questions (what/how/why) and deepen questioning to promote reasoning and sense-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inviting questions to elicit participation, sequence what/how/why questions to deepen understanding, and refine follow-ups to push student thinking without shutting them down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom interaction techniques (be explicit, use your body, hand raising, wait time, multiple hands, everyone shares, think-pair-share)
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-practices teachers use to manage talk, encourage participation, and make expectations explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about participation norms, use body language and movement to engage, employ wait time to allow thinking, use multiple-hands or cold-call strategies equitably, and use think-pair-share or turn-and-talk to surface ideas from more students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting students equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for choosing which students speak or present so that participation is distributed fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repeatedly calling on high-status students; use selection methods (random call, preselection, equitable call lists) tied to participation goals and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning competence is the practice of explicitly elevating the status of students perceived as low status by highlighting their meaningful contributions in public spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public recognition of contributions (spotlight), naming ideas, teacher press, revoicing, and explicit competence statements to raise status and shift participation patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Five Practices (orchestrating whole-class discussions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deliberate sequence of teacher practices for orchestrating student work and whole-class discussion (the Five Practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for and enact practices such as anticipating student responses, monitoring during group work, selecting and sequencing student responses to present, connecting students' contributions, and using purposeful questions to draw out mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-selecting before class
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing specific student work or students to present ahead of class to ensure equitable representation during whole-class discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-select artifacts or students intentionally to highlight diverse strategies and include lower-status voices in public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to conflict and toxic classroom environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and address problematic interactions, microaggressions, and toxic dynamics that harm equitable participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use microintervention strategies, explicit naming, restorative practices, and institutional supports to respond quickly and maintain safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microintervention strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Short, targeted teacher moves to address microaggressions or problematic interactions as they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moves such as explicit naming of behavior, centering harmed students, re-voicing respectful alternatives, and referring to community agreements; integrate with broader restorative practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity Analytics / EQUIP
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUIP is a customizable observation tool for tracking patterns in student participation; equity analytics is the theoretical underpinning which focuses on creating a fair distribution of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EQUIP can be used in real-time or with videos to generate analytics after observations; use disaggregated data to reveal participation patterns across social markers and inform targeted instructional changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Marker Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: A principle of equity analytics stating that data must be disaggregated along social marker identities for it to be useful for reducing inequities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze participation data by race, gender, or other relevant identities so interventions can be targeted (e.g., to improve outcomes for Black students you need data specific to Black students).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Contributions (analytic metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric that accounts for the size of demographic groups: overall contributions for each group divided by the number of students in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use average contributions to compare per-student participation across groups; example: 8 contributions from 4 Black students = average 2; 16 contributions from 20 Latinx students = average 0.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size and statistical measures (Cohen's d, Hedges' g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical measures of the magnitude of differences between groups or pre/post effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohen’s d (difference between means divided by standard deviation) or Hedges’ g for pooled/unequal sample sizes when reporting strength of interventions; interpret alongside practical significance for instructional decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment for learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative assessment strategies designed to inform instruction and promote learning (questioning strategies, rough drafts, opening problems, exit tickets, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use low-stakes checks for understanding, frequent feedback, rough drafts, and exit tickets to monitor learning and adapt instruction; align formative tasks to learning goals and equity aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning strategies for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use questioning to elicit evidence of student understanding as part of assessment for learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design questions that reveal thinking (not just answers), use a mix of conceptual and procedural prompts, and scaffold follow-up questions to probe depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback (direction and practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback is a process in which learners make sense of information about their performance and use it to enhance the quality of their work or learning strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to feedback direction (strengths vs areas for growth), emphasize competence and growth, avoid trivial praise, develop feedback literacy, and structure feedback so students can act on it (timely, specific, actionable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' ability to interpret, use, and act on feedback to improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students how to receive feedback, how to give peer feedback, and provide cycles of revision so feedback leads to concrete improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer- and self-assessment; the assessment cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cycles of initial draft, self-reflection, peer feedback, and revision (peer-assisted reflection) to support learning and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement structured peer feedback protocols, scaffold self-reflection prompts, provide exemplars, and require revision so students practice applying feedback and developing metacognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic summative assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Summative tasks that resemble meaningful, real-world mathematical practice (portfolios, projects, students-as-teachers, multimodal essays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design authentic tasks aligned with learning goals, use rubrics to communicate expectations, allow multimodal evidence of learning, and consider alternatives to traditional timed exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using rubrics in assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubrics provide criteria and levels of performance for summative and formative tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, criterion-based rubrics that emphasize learning goals and provide students with guidance for improvement; combine rubrics with exemplars and calibration activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative grading approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Nontraditional grading systems (standards-based grading, specifications grading, ungrading) intended to address problems with traditional grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand why grading is problematic (e.g., harms motivation, obscures learning), consider standards-based or specifications systems, allow revision and resubmission, or explore ungrading practices while attending to institutional constraints and equity implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolios and projects as assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting student work over time (portfolios) or evaluating extended, authentic projects to assess learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use portfolios and projects to capture learning growth, emphasize process and reflection, and include criteria aligned with mathematical practices and equity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students as teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic assessment and learning opportunity where students teach content to peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use teaching assignments to develop metacognition and communication skills; scaffold preparation and assessment so student-led teaching is inclusive and rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal essays and alternative artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow students to demonstrate learning through multiple modes (written, video, oral, visual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about assessment criteria for multimodal work and provide supports for students with different access needs and language backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer feedback protocols and exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured protocols and exemplars used to make peer feedback effective and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train students in giving constructive feedback, use guided prompts, provide rubrics and exemplars, and hold students accountable for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development and collective learning (EQUIP Learning Circle, book clubs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices for instructor learning and change including book clubs, EQUIP learning circles, and collective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sustained, community-based PD with data (EQUIP) to support change; engage in cycles of practice, observation, and reflection; build learning communities to sustain equitable teaching efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting it all together: practice and feedback cycles for instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate cycles of practice, observation, feedback, and reflection for instructors to improve equitable teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use micropractice, peer coaching, observation tools (EQUIP), and learning communities to iterate on instruction and measure impact on participation and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary-defined constructs to evaluate instruction (implicit bias, stereotype threat, status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key constructs that affect classroom equity and should be considered when evaluating practice: implicit bias, stereotype threat, status, microaggressions, teacher immediacy, teacher press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of how these constructs manifest in interactions and data; design interventions that reduce bias, mitigate stereotype threat, redistribute status, and increase teacher immediacy and appropriate teacher press.
